The trend of adults buying toys, frequently ⁢enough‌ referred to‍ as “kidults,” has been growing considerably. This phenomenon⁣ is driven by a blend of nostalgia and ⁢the appealing design of toys, creating a strong emotional connection with⁤ collectors. The market for adult toy collectors is rapidly evolving, influenced by changing demographics ‌and the‍ powerful ⁤impact of nostalgia on ⁣purchasing decisions.
In many countries, the market ‍for adult toys has been expansive ⁢even before ​the pandemic. As an example, in ‍Japan,⁤ this trend is known as “otaku,” and the‍ market for‍ toys targeted at adult collectors has been​ well-established.The ​global toy market⁤ is forecasted to reach $200 billion by 2032, ⁤with collectibles and vintage toys contributing $35 billion of that growth.Notably, more than 19% of toy sales ​in the U.S.⁢ are ​to customers over ⁣the age of 18.
Amanda Hope, a 36-year-old⁤ software specialist from Surrey, is one of the many adults who have embraced this trend. She has spent over £3,000 on her collection of Jellycat soft toys, which she finds ⁢irresistible due to‌ thier cute and cuddly nature. This growing trend highlights the ‍intersection⁣ of childhood memories and contemporary design, making toys an appealing ‌collectible⁤ item for ⁤adults.
The Rise of Adult Toy Collectors: A New Trend on tiktok and beyond In ‍the ever-evolving world ‌of social media, a peculiar trend has emerged on ‍platforms like TikTok. Adults are increasingly turning⁢ to⁤ toys and ​collectibles as a form of ⁢self-care and mental health relief. From Jellycats to Lego plastic bricks and ‍ Sonny ‍Angels dolls , ‍these toys are ‌not just for ⁢children anymore. The phenomenon⁤ has sparked a wave ⁤of unboxing ‌videos and ⁣purchases, ⁤with one in five toys and games now⁣ bought by over-18s for themselves,⁤ according to Circana , a leading toy industry research group.
The Mental⁢ Health Benefits of Collectibles The research conducted ⁣by Circana found that buying collectibles had positive mental⁤ health benefits. These toys ⁢provide a sense of nostalgia and comfort, helping adults cope with the turmoil of everyday life. From Jellycat ‘s whimsical plush toys to Lego ‘s intricate building sets, these items⁣ offer a creative outlet and ⁣a way to unwind.
The ⁤Impact on the⁢ Toy Industry The Jellycat craze,⁤ in‌ particular,‍ has⁤ made a significant⁢ impact on⁤ the toy industry. These plush toys,ranging from eggs with faces ‍to smiley coffee cups,have become highly sought after. Similarly, a TikTok trend ‌for unboxing ‍ Sonny ‌Angels has put these tiny dolls in high‍ demand. the popularity ‍of these​ toys has led ​to‍ increased‍ sales and a renewed⁢ interest in collectibles among adults.
The Cost ‍of Collecting While these toys can bring joy ⁤and relaxation,they don’t⁣ come cheap. Jellycats ⁢range in price from £11 to over £700, and Lego gift sets for ⁢adults can cost as much as £730. Despite the ‍high‍ prices, many adults are willing to spend their disposable ​income‍ on these collectibles.
Why Adults Are Spending on Toys So, why are so many adults spending their money on toys?⁣ The answer lies in⁣ the⁤ emotional and mental benefits these items provide. For many, collecting toys is a way to ⁤escape the ⁢stresses of ⁣adult life and reconnect with simpler times. The act of⁣ purchasing and collecting these items can also provide a sense of accomplishment ⁤and satisfaction.
The Future of Adult⁢ Collecting As the ‍trend continues⁢ to grow, it will be ‍interesting to see how the toy industry adapts. Companies may start to cater ​more specifically to adult collectors, offering more sophisticated and high-quality ⁣items. ‌Additionally, social media platforms like TikTok will ​likely continue to play a significant ‍role⁢ in promoting these trends and connecting collectors.

The ‌Therapeutic Power of Lego: A Young’s Journey In the bustling ​world of⁣ today, ​finding ways ‌to unwind and destress is more significant than ever. For ⁢23-year-old Elle Lynn, the ​solution lies in the simple ‌yet engaging world of Lego. ‍With her black-framed ‌glasses and long dark hair,⁣ Elle exudes a calm confidence, a trait that is evident in ‍her approach to collecting and building‌ Lego sets.
Elle’s journey into the world of Lego ‍began as a⁢ means to ‌escape ⁤the pressures of her high-stress job as a project coordinator.”I find⁣ it quite ​therapeutic to build,” she ‌says. “It‌ helps me switch off from a ‍busy high-stress day.” This sentiment resonates with⁢ many adults who find ⁢solace in the tactile and creative ‍process of ‌assembling Lego pieces.
Elle ‍estimates she has spent ​around £500 on her lego collection, a figure that coudl be higher if not for the cost of larger sets.”For some of the larger Lego ​sets they do tend to come at a larger price‌ so they aren’t‍ as easily attainable,” she explains. The cost of Lego⁢ sets can ‍indeed be⁢ a‌ barrier, but for many, the benefits far outweigh the expenses.Lego has long been ‌recognized for its therapeutic benefits.‍ The act of building can reduce stress and‍ anxiety, improve fine motor skills,⁣ and enhance ‌problem-solving abilities. ​According to ​a study ‍published​ in the ‌ Journal of Play , Lego⁤ play can also boost creativity and self-esteem.
Elle’s⁤ collection is not limited to lego alone. She also collects Jellycats,a brand known for its soft,cuddly‌ toys. The combination of these two hobbies offers her a dual form of‍ relaxation—one tactile and creative, the other soft and⁣ comforting.
The Cost ⁢of Collecting While Elle​ enjoys her ‍Lego collection, she acknowledges ​the financial ‍aspect. “I would probably have more Lego if it weren’t for the cost,” she says. This is a common challenge‍ for‌ collectors.Lego sets can range from a few pounds to hundreds, depending on their size and ​complexity. For those⁤ interested in starting a collection,budgeting and prioritizing sets can be crucial.

For⁣ those considering starting‌ their own collection, Elle’s advice is simple: “Start with what⁣ you ​love and build from there.”
Lego has evolved significantly over ⁤the years, offering a wide ​range of themes and sets that cater to various interests. from Star⁤ Wars to Harry⁤ Potter, there’s⁣ a Lego set for everyone. This diversity makes ‍it easier for collectors to find sets that resonate⁢ with their personal interests and passions.
Conclusion Elle Lynn’s story is ⁣a testament to the therapeutic ​power of Lego.
